# CHD-3.1 → BUILD-SPEC REV 1.1 — REVISION PLAN
``` DOC : review/PLAN.md DATE : 2026-11-09 INPUT : review/chd31-package/ (7 files: 00-START-HERE, 01-AUTHORING-BRIEF, 02-WORKFLOW-SUITE, 03-REVISION-HANDOFF, 04-DETAILED-FEEDBACK, 05-REVIEW-LOG.json canonical, 06-SOURCE-MANIFEST) TARGET : build-spec/ rev 1.1 (INDEX.md + VOL-A..D, new VOL-E, new VOL-F) + contracts/ + acceptance/ STATUS : PLAN ONLY. No rendering, no PDF work, no code, no deployment, no external messages. This file is the instruction for the authoring task; it is not itself the authored specification. ```
---

## 0. What this plan decides
1. **Every one of the 30 stable findings (R31-001..R31-030) is mapped to the build-spec volume and section that must change**, with the change type (correction / new content / rewrite / package-level). 2. **Every user decision is carried or applied** — D-001..D-016 as already integrated in rev 1.0, D-017..D-038 as revision decisions, with D-038 (fork permission policy) specified to the level the author needs. 3. **The target document structure is fixed** along the authoring brief's A–P section plan: coherent subsystem/function groups, not one sheet per section, with page-range estimates that are planning aids and never caps. 4. **Each volume section is classified** as new content or correction, so the author does not re-derive scope.
Nothing here closes a finding by citing an identifier. Each row names what must exist after the edit and how a reviewer proves it exists.
---

### 1.2 Authority order (highest first)
1. User decisions **D-017..D-038** (live review, 9 Nov 2026), and D-038 for the fork policy specifically. 2. User decisions **D-001..D-016** where not contradicted by 1. 3. Stable findings **R31-001..R31-030** (correction + completion evidence). 4. Prior review-log items (RL-n, CT-n, R-n, FACT-n) as cited by `DESIGN.md` rev 3.0. 5. Reviewer proposals in the authoring brief and workflow suite — including every page allowance, the operation-card template, the ten scenarios, and all suggested mechanisms. 6. Current build-spec rev 1.0 text — authoritative only where 1–5 are silent.
When two sources conflict, the higher source wins and the author records a one-line supersession note at the affected section. Silent reconciliation is a defect: the reader must be able to see which rule displaced which.

### 1.3 Terminology fixed once (brief §A acceptance)
The revised package defines these once, in VOL-A §1.3, and every volume links to that definition instead of re-defining:
`VP` · `director` · `manager` · `supervisor` · `foreman` · `worker` · `room` · `thread` · `task` · `ticket` · `workflow` · `session` · `fork` · `bond` · `attempt` · `run` · `gateway request` · `send` · `report` · `dataset` · `grant` · `meta-grant` · `snapshot` · `archive` · `checkpoint` · `restore` · `lease` · `admission` · `enqueue-only` · `run-now`.
Two distinctions must survive into every later section:
- **send ≠ attempt ≠ gateway request.** A logical send may be attempted more than once, including against a fresh session; a gateway request is one POST. - **fork ≠ delivery mode.** Fork provisions a native session; delivery selects NEW or REUSE for a wake. Fork is never a third delivery mode.

### 1.4 What this plan does not authorize
No repository edits, no boardctl/Hermes implementation changes, no deployment, no external messages, no claim of owner acceptance, no rendering. The workflow suite's vendor research documents promoted patterns, not CHD capabilities; the Sentry case is vendor-hosted self-report.

### 3.3 D-038 — the fork / session-permission policy, specified
The brief requires the author to define activation, readback, lineage, atomicity, and in-flight behavior. The plan fixes the shape; the author implements it consistently across config, records, API, and tests.
**Policy switch (author-proposed identifiers, as the user supplied policy and not names):**
``` sessions.fork_policy: "preserve_parent_snapshot" | "current_policy" default: "preserve_parent_snapshot" scope: global default with per-agent override; a per-project override may narrow, never widen, the VP setting activation: at fork creation and at explicit resync; never retroactive to existing sessions ```
**Snapshot record** (`SessionPolicySnapshot`, new, VOL-B §3.11):
``` { snapshot_id, session_id, parent_session_id?, fork_mode, agent, profile, policy_rev, captured_at, grants: [{capability, resource_scope, class, origin, grant_id?}], superseded_by? } ```
- Written at session creation and at every fork. - `fork_mode = preserve_parent_snapshot` → child inherits `parent.snapshot_id` and `policy_rev` verbatim. Revoked-derived rights remain effective for that session (D-033, D-038 default). - `fork_mode = current_policy` → child resolves grants against current VP configuration and current grant records; `policy_rev` = current revision. - Existing sessions never silently re-resolve because a tool call happened. This is the "no automatic refresh under preserve-parent mode" rule.
**Resync operation** (author-proposed identifier):
``` POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/policy-resync (service tool: chd_session_policy_resync) body: { expected_policy_rev, reason, approval_ref? } authorization: the agent's own session-policy authority, or a grant of session.policy_resync from a holder with that authority effect: new snapshot revision (policy_rev + 1) computed from current policy; single audited record write; readback confirms denial: 403 policy_resync_not_granted (audited) ```
- Atomicity: one snapshot-revision record write; either the new revision is committed and readable, or nothing changed. No partial grant set. - Readback: `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/policy` returns effective snapshot, `policy_rev`, origins, and the fork mode that produced it. - In-flight: tool calls already authorized continue under the snapshot they were authorized against; the new revision applies at the next authorization boundary. A resync during an in-flight call is not retroactive. - Restart: same session id keeps its snapshot. Replacement restore imports the archived snapshot record; if it is absent, the restore fails closed to `current_policy` **with a recorded `snapshot_missing` decision** — never a silent choice. - Denial/limits: resync cannot widen beyond the agent's configured `use` pool; it can only remove revoked-derived rights or pick up newly granted ones within that pool.
**Test variants (added to WF-08 and the common session-policy tests):**
1. Revoke an ancestor grant, then fork under the default → child retains the parent snapshot. 2. Fork under `current_policy` → child excludes revoked-derived rights. 3. Explicit authorized resync → `policy_rev` advances; readback shows the new revision; audit row exists. 4. Resync without authority → documented denial, audited, no change. 5. New tool calls on an untouched session → no silent refresh. 6. Restart and replacement restore → snapshot preserved, or fail-closed with `snapshot_missing` recorded.

The authoring handoff is accepted only when all of the following hold, and each is checkable by a reviewer without reading the author's intent:
1. **30/30 findings** have a disposition: the section changed, the requirement ids added/edited, and the completion test that proves it. No finding is marked closed because an id is cited; no finding is silently dropped. 2. **D-001..D-038 all traced**; superseded assumptions (§3.4) have no surviving occurrence anywhere in the package, verified by a text search. 3. **D-038 implemented** across config, record, API, readback, restore, and tests, with the six variants of §3.3 present in `acceptance/` (WF-08 and the common session-policy tests). 4. **Structure** follows §5: coherent subsystem sections, continuation headings, one authoritative contract per entity, no sheet-per-section layout, and no text shrunk to fit a page. 5. **Requirement ids** are contiguous per family, unique, and every id cited in prose exists. INDEX carries the id→file→section map. 6. **Contract consistency**: one message-kind enum; one public error contract (`404` indistinguishable, no `403 forbidden` for membership); enums and HTTP codes agree across volume text, tables, tools, and contracts; role matrices agree with allowed supervisor/foreman actions. 7. **Keys and states**: no `/chd/...` key written without its leading slash; one canonical state machine per entity; cancellation and resume drawn; waiting is not terminal-and-resumable at once. 8. **Ten workflows** (WF-01..WF-10) represented with fixtures, ordered actions, field-level expected records, evidence queries, failure branches, cleanup, and pass rules. Vendor research and proposed scope are labelled as such; no vendor parity is claimed. 9. **Contracts are actual**: every schema, endpoint, error, and config field the volume text references exists in `contracts/` with types, limits, defaults, and absence semantics. A cited id with no content behind it is a defect (the finding that started this revision). 10. **Honest status**: implemented / measured / proposed / unverified are labelled separately. A green build, page count, requirement count, or passing fixture is never reported as semantic, deployment, or owner acceptance (IDX-003, VOLD-046). 11. **OPEN register refreshed**: 25 carried items with status, plus N-1..N-8 marked "PROPOSED — not user-confirmed". No open item is closed by an invented default. 12. **No rendering in this phase.** The author returns normative text, schemas, fixtures, and figure specifications; the rendered handbook is a separate, later task driven by this structure.

## 9. Plan-level decisions and risks
**Decisions taken by this plan (not user policy):**
- **Keep the four-volume spine and its ids.** VOL-A..D stay the authoritative files; corrections happen in place. This avoids renumbering 211 volume requirements and preserves the rev 1.0 verification record. - **Two new volumes only.** Tickets (VOL-E) and session archives/restore (VOL-F) are genuinely new subsystems with no existing home; everything else extends an existing volume. A new volume is cheaper to review than a 40-page insertion into VOL-B or VOL-C. - **VOL-D becomes a five-part volume.** Provisioning, reports, and federation would otherwise push it past readability. Parts keep one file until the ~2,800-line threshold, then split with ids unchanged. - **Relocated ids keep their names.** If a requirement must move files, the id follows it and INDEX maps both; ids are lineage labels, not location labels. - **D-038 identifiers are proposed, not user-supplied.** `sessions.fork_policy`, `SessionPolicySnapshot`, and the resync operation are named here so the author does not invent conflicting names in four volumes. - **Where the PDF and the build-spec disagree, the finding's required change wins.** Where a finding and a decision disagree, the decision wins; the conflict is recorded at the section, not resolved silently.
**Risks and mitigations:**
| Risk | Mitigation | |---|---| | VOL-D overgrows and becomes unreadable | Five parts with part-level estimates; split threshold; figure specs extracted to Pt V | | Archive/restore depends on an unsupplied native export schema | Capability probe + version pin; mark dependency; no invented format; fail-closed `snapshot_missing` analogue for restore | | Dataset/table support is unreleased in DuckBrain | Explicit CHD logical records + adapter contract; do not assume a native feature | | Admission ownership (N-1) is a real design fork | One proposal with reversible default, atomic reservation rule, race test; marked proposed | | Author drifts into implementation or rendering | §1.4 and §8.12: no code, no PDF, no deployment, no acceptance claims | | Findings closed by citation | §8.1 and the completion test column; INDEX table must name the proving artifact | | Stale contradictory text survives an edit | §3.4 supersession list becomes a post-edit text search |

## 10. Out of scope
- Rendering the handbook, PDF generation, print, layout QA at reading scale (a later task consumes this structure). - Repository edits: Hermes, DuckBrain, boardctl, Crier, scheduler. - Deployment, live adapters, credentials, external messages, owner sign-off. - Rebooting the ten workflows into ten domain products; they test primitives. - Filling any open item with an invented default. - Editing `AGENTS.md` in any project, and any claim that the reviewed PDF's missing external volumes were consulted.
